text.tspan: Figure 2 Waveform class, response timing, and cue direction
Waveform identity uses a stable purple-yellow grammar; functional response and recording area retain separate encodings.
Normalized extracellular waveforms and waveform feature space
The yellow waveform, yellow feature-space points, purple waveform, and purple feature-space points are explicitly linked by class.
Four equal-height vertical bars show within-area proportions; both segment counts and percentages are printed inside.
Cue-response time courses and latency by waveform class
One six-trace panel shows M2, M1, and S1 means +/- 1 SD for both waveform classes. The unit-level latency map is retained below.
Responsive-unit composition: waveform class by cue direction
Four scope-specific two-by-two count tables cross waveform class with one-SD cue direction; neutral-band units are excluded.
